Full (R), (L), (E) checks ran only where |K| <= 1500: K2 and K3 at p=2 and p=3. C4, K4, C5 at p=3 (|K| = 6561 to 59049): (L) and (E) NOT checked; greedy-sparse family not built. structure.summary: T11-C (verified exact computation, PI own engine): rectangular Kronecker coefficients g(lambda,(d^n),(d^n)) for lambda |- nd, computed exactly via Murnaghan-Nakayama characters + class-sum formula. Determinant-side closure multiplicity satisfies delta_lambda <= g(lambda,(d^n),(d^n)); so the VANISHING locus {lambda : g=0} is exactly where delta_lambda=0, i.e. the only places a padded-permanent occurrence obstruction (gamma_lambda>0=delta_lambda) can live. Results: (n=2,d=3) and (n=3,d=2), N=6: 7 of 11 partitions vanish, identical sets {(5,1),(4,1,1),(3,3),(3,2,1),(2,2,1,1),(2,1^4),(1^6)} (consistency: (2,2,2)'=(3,3) + Kronecker conjugation symmetry). (n=3,d=3) N=9: 13/30 vanish. (n=4,d=2) N=8: 15/22 vanish. (n=2,d=4) N=8: 15/22 vanish.

structure.text: REPLICATION (exploratory, not a proof, not independent of cm-e7f2bb5242ff4b60: same design, same model family). Fresh seed 20261123, positive 1-in-3 random CNFs, n=10,12,14,16, T=20 instances per point. DFS over 0/1 assignments with GF(3)-affine feasibility pruning at every prefix, checked against brute force on the same instances: mismatches=0 at all points (exactness holds). density 0.5 (m~n/2): mean_checks 216.4 / 441.2 / 758.1 / 1443.7, log2-slope n=10..16 = 0.456; frac_sat 0.95-1.0. density 1.0 (m=n): mean_checks 9.4 / 13.9 / 9.0 / 14.1, log2-slope = 0.097; frac_sat 0.1-0.3; blind_among_gf3 rises 0.20 / 0.50 / 0.75 / 0.67 (blind = GF(3)-feasible but no 0/1 solution; denominator is GF(3)-feasible instances, NOT all instances, so it is not comparable to the earlier ~0.9% figure). Prediction H1 (density-0.5 slope ~0.4-0.5, density-1.0 slope clearly below 1) matched in direction; competing H0 (slope 1, brute-force-like) not excluded at density 0.5 by this data because T=20 gives no confidence intervals. Surprise: at density 1.0 the GF(3) filter is weak (most feasible instances are blind), so the pruning cost is not explained by GF(3) rank alone. Open: the slope estimates are not statistically established; the measure is first-solution search at density 0.5, not a #SAT count; no speed-up claim is supported until larger T with intervals.

statement: VERIFICATION (independent re-implementation of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 d-ary tree bookkeeping, n=2..12, d in {2,4,8}, 2^n leaves). Result: max_fanout = 1 on all visible rows, i.e. every description and every Circuit-Min-Merge gate output feeds exactly one parent gate, so the gate DAG is a tree. Prediction-formula errors (my own, not the construction): I used layers = n // log2(d) and gates = (2^n - 1)/(d-1), which hold only for exact powers of d. Scope: bookkeeping of the tree shape only. It does NOT decide the K1 gap (whether the MMW19 family has depth/reuse structure that yields the required formula-size bound under NP subset P/poly), and it is not a P vs NP step.

statement: For every finite simple graph G, tw(G[K_2]) = 2*tw(G)+1, where G[K_2] is the lexicographic product of G with K_2 (vertices (v,i) with i∈{0,1}; adjacency defined as a~b or (a=b and i≠j)).

candidate.attack: Check the bramble conditions on arbitrary G by constructing the family and proving the hitting-set lower bound; also verify the upper bound via the doubling-bag construction.
candidate.definitions: G[K_2] = lexicographic product of G with K_2; vertices (v,i) for v∈V(G), i∈{0,1}; (a,i)~(b,j) iff a~b or (a=b and i≠j).
candidate.derivation: 1. Let 𝔅 be a bramble of G of order q = tw(G)+1 (Seymour-Thomas). 2. In H = G[K_2] the set {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} is connected because each B×{i} induces a copy of G[B]. 3. If B and B' touch in G, then B×{i} and B'×{j} share a vertex or have an edge in H, and B×{0} and B×{1} are adjacent via edges (a,0)-(a,1). 4. Any hitting set X of this family must satisfy |X_i| ≥ q for each i, hence |X| ≥ 2q, so the bramble order is at least 2q and tw(H) ≥ 2q-1 = 2·tw(G)+1. 5. The standard doubling-bag upper bound replaces each bag X_t by X_t×{0,1}, yielding width 2·tw(G)+1. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2·tw(G)+1 exactly.
candidate.known_closest: The general identity tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1)−1 for lexicographic products with cliques K_n is stated in the literature (e.g., Bodlaender 1998) but not verified for K_2.
candidate.novelty: Provides a bramble-based constructive proof for the lower bound tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 and combines it with the standard doubling-bag upper bound to establish exact equality.
candidate.obstacle: Verify that the family {B×{i} : B∈𝔅, i∈{0,1}} satisfies the bramble conditions (connectedness, touching) in H and that any hitting set X must have size at least 2(tw(G)+1) for arbitrary G.
candidate.target_relevance: Closes the lower-bound part of the width-theorem obligation S0018, which requires proving tw(G[K_2]) ≥ 2·tw(G)+1 for all G.

Exploratory held-out observation, not a proof; no claim submitted.

statement: Exhaustive n=6 enumeration (all 2^20 triple-sets, experiment cm-7e1dbca3747b4714): among d-regular positive 1-in-3 instances (every variable in exactly d clauses) the satisfiable and unsatisfiable counts are (d,m)=(1,2): 10 sat/0 unsat; (2,4): 75/0; (3,6): 300/30; (4,8): 285/495; (5,10): 90/954; (6,12): 15/765; (7,14): 0/330; (8,16): 0/75; (9,18): 0/10; (10,20): 0/1. Two findings. (a) Sufficiency of d | m is FALSE: the instances (3,6) and (4,8) are unsatisfiable although d divides m. (b) The necessity check 'sat implies d | m' gave 0 violations, but at n=6 every d-regular instance has m = 2d (since 6d = 3m), so d | m holds automatically and the check is vacuous. It does not test the divisibility necessity. The necessity itself is a proof (counting), so the test is only meaningful at n where n*d/3 is not a multiple of d, e.g. n=7, d=3, m=7 (Fano).

statement: D-016e: Cycle RC-0bd8fd6a (cm in research-atlas.jsonl): C mod 2 = covering parity (number of choices, per clause, of a singleton or the full triple whose union is all n variables, mod 2); checked 777/777. Proof (director, 3 lines): over GF(2) the exactly-one indicator of a clause abc is a+b+c+abc (from a+b+c-2(ab+ac+bc)+3abc); so C = sum_x prod_clauses(...) mod 2; expanding chooses one term per clause, giving the monomial x^U with U the union; sum_x x^U = 2^(n-|U|), odd iff U = all variables. Not novel (standard GF(2) polynomial counting); valid as a reformulation. The run's second part (does the inclusion-exclusion table cost track the frontier-DP state count) is not assessed here. 2026-11-18

Minimality uses the containment check on 4-subsets, which suffices because an unsat 3-subset would make every superset contain an unsat 4-subset.

statement: DISCOVERY (cm-62a40be9abba4b48), reading of TR17-165 Def 3.1 as rank(J⊗A + g⊗B) = rank A + rank(g)·rank B with J the all-ones matrix (reading NOT yet checked against the paper). Exhaustive over 2x2 gadgets g and all A,B in F^{2x2}, over GF(2) and GF(3). (i) Rank-one lemma: rank(J+g)=rank(g)+1 iff the all-ones vector lies in neither col(g) nor row(g); 0 mismatches over all gadgets for r=2,3 at p=2,3. (ii) Def 3.1 test at r=2: GF(2) 5 passing gadgets (ranks 0,1); GF(3) 19 passing gadgets (ranks 0,1); no rank-2 gadget passes at either field. The rank-2 failure is forced by size: rank(J+g) <= 2 for 2x2, so rank(g)+1 <= 2 needs rank(g) <= 1. So the r=2 result is a size artefact, not evidence against a good gadget. Prediction vs outcome: H2 (no full-rank 2x2 pass) matched; H1 (some pass) matched only for rank <= 1, which is trivial. Does not decide the existence of a good gadget with rank(g) >= 2.
